safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce from 4.0 to 3.0 days — safety stock absorbs buffer

narrative: Material PL1__M78165D5 exhibits erratic demand with a coefficient of variation of 0.60 and 88.5% non-zero days, driven by lognormal-shaped variability across the observation period. Lead times average 2.96 working days with a CV of 0.43, making lead-time variance the dominant uncertainty driver (60.9% of total LTD variance). A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is recommended: reorder at 1,231 units and replenish 1,327 units (EOQ), supported by a 588-unit safety stock to achieve the 95% service level target. Capacity utilisation is 44.5%, leaving ample headroom within the 4,306-unit storage limit.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) — continuous review, fixed reorder point and fixed order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic but mostly continuous demand (88.5% non-zero days) with stable ordering cadence is well-suited to a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. The relatively high throughput (35,861 units/year) justifies frequent monitoring, and EOQ balances ordering and holding costs efficiently. An (s,S) policy would add unnecessary complexity without meaningful cost benefit given the demand pattern.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding (1,327 OQ + 588 SS = 1,915 units vs. 4,307 limit; 44.5% utilisation). No capacity-driven order quantity reduction required.
